title: Lake vs Pond + River vs Stream

voice.name: Liam (ElevenLabs default — young, energetic American; works on the free plan)

pauseRule: "pause" = TOTAL silence (seconds) after that line — only on important beats (hook question, topic switch, into recap, before CTA).
artNote: Hook = big animated landscape (intro scene, 950x630): mountain ridge sketches in, a fish jumps in a big lake, a duck bobs on a pond, clouds drift, orange ? marks bob over both. Only pair 1 is teased; river/stream stay a surprise until the topic switch. p1 cards = side cross-sections (deep lake: sun rays stop, bottom dark, fish swims; shallow pond: rays hit the bottom, plants sway). p2 cards = top-down (river: wide, flowing, fed by two streams that draw in, paper boat bobs; stream: narrow, a frog hops and an orange arc shows you can step across).

lines.text: Lake or pond? Most people just guess.
A lake is deep, so its bottom stays dark.
A pond is shallow. Sun hits the whole bottom.
But Walden Pond is over 100 feet deep.
A river is big, fed by smaller streams.
A stream is small and shallow.
The Mississippi starts as a stream you can walk across.
Tip: a river is just a stream that grew up.
